newsitem.title: USA: Winter storm coats Texas, Louisiana in ice.
newsitem.headline: Winter storm coats Texas, Louisiana in ice.

text.p: A winter storm coated much of Texas and Louisiana in a thick sheet of ice on Monday that knocked out electricity to thousands of homes and forced schools and businesses to close across the region.
Police said at least seven people died in weather-related accidents after the ice storm moved in at the weekend, and warned people to stay at home if possible.
"Austin, San Antonio and Houston roadways are completely iced over and particularly hazardous," the Texas Department of Transportation said in a statement.

State officials said 1,000 motorists were stranded overnight about 40 miles (65 km) south of Austin because of ice on Interstate Highway 10. Emergency shelters were set up in nearby towns to house them.
In Houston, drivers spent the night in their cars when they got stuck on an icy overpass and had to wait eight hours for help to arrive.
"We kept calling and trying to get somebody out there ... We just kept the car running (to stay warm)," said motorist Barbara Williams.
Police said virtually the entire Interstate Highway system in Lousiana was closed. "It's an absolute mess out there, really severe for us," said a spokesman for the Louisiana State Police.

Schools, businesses and government offices throughout the region closed on Monday so that people could stay home, but many of them were left to sit in cold and dark houses because of extensive power outages.
At least 250,000 homes in Texas and Louisiana were without electricity on Monday, mostly because of ice-coated tree limbs falling on to power lines, officials said.

Houston Lighting and Power spokesman Graham Painter said repair crews were finding it difficult to fully restore power because so many line breaks were occurring. "It's like chasing your tail," he said.
In Dallas, American Airlines said it would cancel about 200 flights at its hub at Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport.
